correctness.rationale: Normalized angular integration reproduces the known two-factor incomplete-gamma diagonal spectrum. For r_j=Q_(j+1)/Q_j, the convergent series r_j=1-1/(1+sum_(s>=1)x^s/[(j+2)...(j+s+1)]) gives strict increase with x, strict decrease with j, and r_j~x/(j+2). Consecutive eigenvalue ratios consequently decrease with k and cross 1 strictly once apiece, in ordered succession. A product-of-ratios endpoint comparison proves the exact minimum. Uniform interior expansions yield \(k_m=ma/(a+b)+O(1)\); the gamma-tail and Stirling calculations then give the claimed positive sharp exponential and \(m^{-3/2}\) coefficient. All positive radius and m>=1 boundaries, tie multiplicities, and eigenvalue-versus-singular ratio are explicit. Packaged verify.py passed selected independent gamma moment and spectral checks; finite computation is not used as the universal proof.

Relevant primary theory, published-finding corpus examples with different radial or sphere objects, web equivalence/alias searches, and own recoverable claim titles/objects were compared by assumptions and implication. Full-spectrum prior results make general computation possible, but the strict all-mode comparisons and large-degree constant are additional inequalities and asymptotic theorems, not claims covered as an explicitly supplied evaluation. Publication priority remains provisional given unindexed classical special-function and polydisc optimization work.

value.rationale: Finite-dimensional exact observability of total-order two-channel Gaussian-Hermite signals under two independent time-frequency disc cutoffs is a natural concentration problem. The theorem goes beyond diagonal integrals by classifying every transition and its transversality for all m, proving exact worst-mode identity, deriving a continuum threshold profile, and computing a sharp positive polynomial prefactor and exponential rate of worst-case reconstruction instability. These structural features are not merely a relabeling, a tiny finite numerical gain, or a known table recomputation. The scope and potential priority risks are explicit.
